name: Avascular Necrosis / Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head
definition: Ischemic death of bone and marrow in the femoral head that can progress to subchondral fracture, collapse and secondary hip arthritis.

typical: Risk factors include corticosteroid exposure and heavy alcohol use

investigations.principle: Early diagnosis is important because radiographs can be normal.
investigations.MRI: MRI is the most sensitive test for early osteonecrosis.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs show sclerosis, crescent sign, collapse and secondary OA in later stages.

green: Early orthopedic review for joint-preserving options in pre-collapse disease
amber: Core decompression, osteotomy or arthroplasty decisions depend on stage, lesion size, symptoms and patient factors.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Asthi/Majja and Vata-related phenotype may be documented, but AVN staging and orthopedic management remain central.

patientEducation.summary: Ischemic death of bone and marrow in the femoral head that can progress to subchondral fracture, collapse and secondary hip arthritis.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
